    <div class="flex-video widescreen">
  <iframe type="text/html" width="100%" height="100%" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/4wVwtmjaHcE?enablejsapi=1&hl=en_US&rel=0&start=&version=3&wmode=transparent" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" frameborder="0" allowscriptaccess="always" webkitAllowFullScreen="true" wmode="transparent" mode="transparent" class="video-embed"></iframe>
</div>



  <p><span><span>Welcome to the PartyRock Generative AI Hackathon by AWS: a challenge for all builders to get hands-on making generative AI-powered apps. In this challenge, you’ll use PartyRock, an Amazon Bedrock Playground as a fast and fun way to learn about Prompt Engineering and Foundational Models (FMs) to build a functional app with generative AI. Experiment with prompts to build an app based on one of four challenge categories or Remix the featured Side Quest app for more ways to compete! </span></span></p>
<p><a href="https://partyrock.aws/guide/getStarted" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Get started</a> and join the <a href="https://discord.gg/suU8YX2rkx" target="_blank" rel="noopener">AWS Community Discord</a> to run your ideas by other hackers or to get help from the PartyRock team.</p>
<p><img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/AWS%20PartyRock/Disco-resource-300.png" alt="" width="300" height="300"></p>
</article>

      
    <article id="challenge-requirements">
      <div class="section-title bold">
        <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
          Requirements
        </h3>
        <span class="section-title-line"></span>
      </div>

      <div>
        <h4>What to Create</h4>
<p>1. <strong>Create or Remix a PartyRock app</strong> to fit into <span style="text-decoration: underline;">one</span> of the following categories:</p>
<ul>
<li>Interactive Learning Experience - virtual science lab, language lesson, etc;</li>
<li>Creative Assistant - music composition assistance, story idea generator, etc;</li>
<li>Experimental Entertainment - interactive story, Role Playing Games, etc;</li>
<li>Freestyle - any project that doesn’t fall into one of the categories above.</li>
</ul>
<p><span><span> </span><strong>AND/OR</strong></span></p>
<p>2. <strong>Remix Side Quest:</strong> Remix THIS <a title="Remix THIS app" href="https://partyrock.aws/u/banjtheman/CnsW_HHSL/ChatRPG" target="_blank" rel="noopener">community-created ChatRPG app</a> to creatively transform it into something as far from the original as possible</p>
<h4> </h4>
<h4>What to Submit</h4>
<p><img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/AWS%20PartyRock/Disco-list-real-final-300.png" alt=""></p>
<p>No matter which type of Project you submit, you’ll need to include the following: </p>
<ol>
<li>Link to your AWS PartyRock Project </li>
<li>Answer all submission questions</li>
<li>If applicable, link to your community.aws Blog Post (see details below) </li>
<li>Optional, but recommended: ~90-second demo video, record a short video interacting with the app you created on PartyRock. Check out the <a href="https://awspartyrockhackathon.devpost.com/details/inspiration#:~:text=the%20PartyRock%20team.-,INSPIRATION,-While%20a%20demo" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Inspiration tab</a> for ideas and tips on making an awesome demo video.</li>
</ol>
<p> </p>
<p><strong>Bonus: Blog Post Prize</strong> Share your journey and the wider impact of your work through a <a href="https://community.aws" target="_blank" rel="noopener">https://community.aws</a> blog post. Please use the tag '<span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>partyrock-hackathon</strong></span>' and address one or both of the following questions, offering valuable insights into your creative process and the potential influence of your project. The content of your blog post must be materially different than your submission questions. The first 152 Eligible Projects that post an Eligible Blog Post to community.aws. </p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Community Impact:</strong> Describe how your project can positively affect your target community. Discuss the potential benefits, envisioned real-world application, and any plans for encouraging adoption.</li>
<li><strong>Alternative Development Scenario with Amazon Bedrock:</strong> Outline how you would have developed your application using Amazon Bedrock if PartyRock wasn't available. Discuss architectural considerations, model selection, and integration of additional tools or services</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<p><strong>Feedback Survey Prize</strong> After you have experimented with PartyRock and submitted your Project, complete this <a href="https://challengepost.wufoo.com/forms/the-partyrock-gen-ai-hackathon-feedback-survey/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">feedback submission form</a> for a chance to win $500 in AWS Credits. </p>
<p> </p>
<p>See <a href="https://awspartyrockhackathon.devpost.com/rules" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Official Rules</a> for details. </p>

      Judging Criteria
    </h3>
    <span class="section-title-line"></span>
  </div>

  <ul class="no-bullet">
      <li>
        <strong>Applicability</strong><br>
        Clarity of the use case (opportunity addressed)
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Quality of the Application</strong><br>
        How well does your app utilize the features of PartyRock and prompt engineering?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Potential to Inspire</strong><br>
        Will the app inspire other users to make creative and entertaining apps?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Creativity</strong><br>
        How original is the idea? Does it address a potentially valuable use case?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Entertainment Value</strong><br>
        Is the app engaging and fun to interact with?
      </li>
  </ul>

  "description": "<p><span></span></p>\n<p>We know Flutter devs love a good challenge, so just in time for the new year to really get going, we’re super excited to announce the next Flutter challenge!&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>\n<p><img src="https://res.cloudinary.com/devpost/image/fetch/s--q1EobgR---/c_limit,f_auto,fl_lossy,q_auto:eco,w_900/https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/780e0e64d323aad2cdd5.png" alt="" width="105" height="59" data-canonical-url="https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/780e0e64d323aad2cdd5.png"><a href="http://flutter.dev/global-gamers">The Global Gamers Challenge</a> is an 8-week contest to design, build, and publish sustainable games, sponsored by Flutter and Global Citizen.&nbsp; Inspired by the mission of the United Nations-facilitated Playing for the Planet Alliance, which Google joined in 2023, international advocacy organization Global Citizen and Flutter, Google’s open-source framework for building multi-platform applications are partnering to host the Global Gamers Challenge.&nbsp;</p>\n<p><strong>What are sustainable games?</strong></p>\n<p><span>Sustainable games use the power of play to inspire positive environmental action. Here are some more ideas inspired by Global Citizen campaigns running right now!</span></p>\n<p><em><span>Encourage a reduction in home energy use</span></em></p>\n<ul>\n<li><span>Data shows that American homes use an average 3x more kwh than the average home across the rest of the globe. Can you build a game that helps to reduce people’s reliance on inefficient energy sources?</span></li>\n</ul>\n<p><em>Encourage a reduction in use of single-use plastics</em></p>\n<ul>\n<li><span>Southeast Asia has some of the highest levels of plastic pollution in the world.       <article id="challenge-description">

  <p><span></span></p>
<p>We know Flutter devs love a good challenge, so just in time for the new year to really get going, we’re super excited to announce the next Flutter challenge!   </p>
<p><img src="https://res.cloudinary.com/devpost/image/fetch/s--q1EobgR---/c_limit,f_auto,fl_lossy,q_auto:eco,w_900/https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/780e0e64d323aad2cdd5.png" alt="" width="105" height="59" data-canonical-url="https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/780e0e64d323aad2cdd5.png"><a href="http://flutter.dev/global-gamers">The Global Gamers Challenge</a> is an 8-week contest to design, build, and publish sustainable games, sponsored by Flutter and Global Citizen.  Inspired by the mission of the United Nations-facilitated Playing for the Planet Alliance, which Google joined in 2023, international advocacy organization Global Citizen and Flutter, Google’s open-source framework for building multi-platform applications are partnering to host the Global Gamers Challenge. </p>
<p><strong>What are sustainable games?</strong></p>
<p><span>Sustainable games use the power of play to inspire positive environmental action. Imagine Candy Crush, but instead of crushing candies, you're crushing plastic pollution! Or picture a game like </span><a href="https://superdash.flutter.dev/"><span>Super Dash</span></a><span>, but instead of</span><span> collecting acorns, you're turning off lights left on</span><span>. Here are some more ideas inspired by Global Citizen campaigns running right now!</span></p>
<p><em><span>Encourage a reduction in home energy use</span></em></p>
<ul>
<li><span>Data shows that American homes use an average 3x more kwh than the average home across the rest of the globe. Can you build a game that helps to reduce people’s reliance on inefficient energy sources?</span></li>
</ul>
<p><em>Encourage a reduction in use of single-use plastics</em></p>
<ul>
<li><span>Southeast Asia has some of the highest levels of plastic pollution in the world. Consider building a game that encourages players to make swaps to reduce reliance on single-use plastics.</span></li>
</ul>
<p><em>Encourage use of public transportation and overland options for longer distances</em></p>
<ul>
<li><span>Europe is home to many of the world’s greatest public transportation systems. Effective games can encourage people to use public transit rather than overland transport, like taking the train rather than flying for longer distances.</span></li>
</ul>
<p><span></span></p>
<p><span>Just like Global Citizens do every day, we’re confident that games can encourage players to take small actions for the environment that when done collectively, lead to a large impact.  </span></p>
<p><strong>Tips on Getting Started!</strong></p>
<p><strong><img src="https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/Flutter/Flutter_GlobalCitizen_GlobalGamers_SectionGraphics_SuperDash_001.png" alt="" width="50" height="69">    SUPER DASH</strong></p>
<p>Play Super Dash, a game we built to inspire you for this challenge. Help Dash capture the golden feather and watch nature be restored as she avoids enemies!</p>
<p><strong><img src="https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/Emojis/music.png" alt="" width="50" height="50">  PRIZES</strong></p>
<p><span>Winners will receive a trip to NYC in September 2024 to meet the Flutter team for a day of workshops and mentorship followed by the opportunity to celebrate their achievements with up to 60,000 other Global Citizens at Global Citizen Festival 2024! </span></p>
<p><strong><img src="https://s3.amazonaws.com/devpost-public/Flutter/Favicon_Wallet.png" alt="" width="50" height="43">  GOOGLE WALLET CHALLENGE</strong></p>
<p>If you’re up for extra credit, we’ve partnered with Google Wallet to offer an additional challenge to deploy an innovative integration of the Google Wallet API in your game. For eligible apps that feature Google Wallet, you will have a chance to win up to $30,000! </p>
<p> </p>
<p><span style="       text-decoration: none;  "><span><span>Whether you’re a Flutter developer who’s new to games, a game developer who is new to Flutter, or new to both game development and Flutter, you’re bound to learn something new while creating a positive impact on the world!</span></span></span></p>
</article>

      
    <article id="challenge-requirements">
      <div class="section-title bold">
        <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
          Requirements
        </h3>
        <span class="section-title-line"></span>
      </div>

      <div>
        <h4>What to Build:</h4>
<p><span></span></p>
<p>Build a game using Flutter and Dart with environmental sustainability content.</p>
<h4>What to Submit:</h4>
<ul>
<li>Include an Application built with the required developer tools.</li>
<li>Include a text description that should explain the features and functionality of your Application.</li>
<li>Include a demonstration video of your Application. The video portion of the submission:
<ul>
<li>should be approximately one (1) minute</li>
<li>should include footage that shows the Application functioning on the device for which it was built</li>
<li>must be uploaded to and made publicly visible on YouTube as a YouTube Short and a link to the video must be provided on the submission form on the Contest Site; and</li>
<li>cannot contain any content, element, or material that violates a third party’s publicity, privacy or intellectual property rights.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Access must be provided to an entrant’s working Application for judging and testing by providing a link to a website, functioning demo, or a test build. If an entrant's code repository is private, entrant must include login credentials in its testing instructions. The Application must be public. </li>
<li>Written and video parts of Entries must be in English.</li>
<li>For the Google Wallet Bonus prize, submissions must include integrations with the Google Wallet API.</li>
</ul>

      <article id="judging-criteria">
  <div class="section-title bold">
    <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
      Judging Criteria
    </h3>
    <span class="section-title-line"></span>
  </div>

  <ul class="no-bullet">
      <li>
        <strong>Overall execution</strong><br>
        Projects will be evaluated based on whether they are responsive to screen size changes, can work with different modes of play (trackpad, mouse, keyboard, and touch for mobile web), and accessibility.


      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Use of animation</strong><br>
        Projects will be evaluated based on the visual appeal and implementation of animation widgets.
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Originality</strong><br>
        Projects will be evaluated based on uniqueness and creativity. Include an innovative and engaging game concept.


      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Best potential value to the community</strong><br>
        Project submissions will be evaluated based on the quality of any tutorials or additional content provided that has the potential to enrich the Flutter community. This includes but is not limited to educational materials, demos, product feedback, etc. 
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Use of environmental sustainability content</strong><br>
        Projects will be evaluated based on relevance to the theme of sustainability and global impact.
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Multiplatform</strong><br>
        Projects that are deployed to multiple platforms will be evaluated based on their quality across all platforms.
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Impact</strong><br>
        Does your game have potential for real-world impact? Does your game build community and encourage interactions?
      </li>
  </ul>
</article>

  "description": " \n<h5 id="reimagine-education-in-the-era-of-ai">\n<span>Reimagine Education in the Era of AI.</span>&nbsp;</h5>\n \n \n<p>The current wave of AI innovation is built on top of a foundation of data, and even the best AI models are only as good as the data being used.</p>\n<p>Microsoft wants to empower the next generation to be fluent not only in AI, but in the database foundations that dictate what algorithms are built and how they are used.&nbsp;</p>\n<p>In that spirit, Microsoft is thrilled to announce the <a href="https://educationblog.microsoft.com/en-us/2023/10/microsofts-ai-classroom-university-hackathon-a-global-challenge-for-students" target="_blank" rel="noopener">“AI Classroom” University Hackathon</a>, a call to students worldwide to reimagine the Future of Education using Azure AI and Azure Databases.&nbsp;</p>\n<p>Join students worldwide in building “intelligent applications” or solutions that use AI as a component of the experience. Full blown apps, prototypes, reference applications or schematic models are all welcome as submissions.&nbsp;</p>\n<p>During this hackathon, you will have support and the resources to learn how to select a database, how to integrate AI in a technical or non-technical solution, and how to build an app using Azure AI and Azure Data Services.&nbsp;</p>\n \n \n<h5 id="why-education">\n<span>Why Education?</span>&nbsp;</h5>\n \n \n<p>AI is changing the world we live in in real-time, and nowhere will this change be more pronounced than for the next generation. How those next generations learn, and what technology is at their disposal, is one of the single biggest influences on the future we share.&nbsp;</p>\n<p>Microsoft wants hackers to have the knowledge and resources to not only innovate—but to think big.&nbsp;</p>\n \n \n<p><strong>$11,000 in prizes are up for grabs </strong>along with the opportunity for mentorship within Microsoft, promotion on Microsoft owned and operated social channels, and have the opportunity to present their projects directly to executives.&nbsp;</p>\n \n<h4 id="what-you-get" class="h2-title">\n<img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/Microsoft/getstartedrobot.png" alt="" width="100" height="100">What you Get</h4>\n<ul>\n<li>Try out AI functionality&nbsp;</li>\n<li>Gain experience with Azure&nbsp;</li>\n<li>Learn from the leaders at Microsoft&nbsp;</li>\n</ul>\n<h4 id="get-started" class="h2-title">\n<img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/Microsoft/getstartedrocket2.png" <h5 id="reimagine-education-in-the-era-of-ai">
<span>Reimagine Education in the Era of AI.</span> </h5>
 
 
<p>The current wave of AI innovation is built on top of a foundation of data, and even the best AI models are only as good as the data being used.</p>
<p>Microsoft wants to empower the next generation to be fluent not only in AI, but in the database foundations that dictate what algorithms are built and how they are used. </p>
<p>In that spirit, Microsoft is thrilled to announce the <a href="https://educationblog.microsoft.com/en-us/2023/10/microsofts-ai-classroom-university-hackathon-a-global-challenge-for-students" target="_blank" rel="noopener">“AI Classroom” University Hackathon</a>, a call to students worldwide to reimagine the Future of Education using Azure AI and Azure Databases. </p>
<p>Join students worldwide in building “intelligent applications” or solutions that use AI as a component of the experience. Full blown apps, prototypes, reference applications or schematic models are all welcome as submissions. </p>
<p>During this hackathon, you will have support and the resources to learn how to select a database, how to integrate AI in a technical or non-technical solution, and how to build an app using Azure AI and Azure Data Services. </p>
 
 
<h5 id="why-education">
<span>Why Education?</span> </h5>
 
 
<p>AI is changing the world we live in in real-time, and nowhere will this change be more pronounced than for the next generation. How those next generations learn, and what technology is at their disposal, is one of the single biggest influences on the future we share. </p>
<p>Microsoft wants hackers to have the knowledge and resources to not only innovate—but to think big. </p>
 
 
<p><strong>$11,000 in prizes are up for grabs </strong>along with the opportunity for mentorship within Microsoft, promotion on Microsoft owned and operated social channels, and have the opportunity to present their projects directly to executives. </p>
 
<h4 id="what-you-get" class="h2-title">
<img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/Microsoft/getstartedrobot.png" alt="" width="100" height="100">What you Get</h4>
<ul>
<li>Try out AI functionality </li>
<li>Gain experience with Azure </li>
<li>Learn from the leaders at Microsoft </li>
</ul>
<h4 id="get-started" class="h2-title">
<img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/Microsoft/getstartedrocket2.png" alt="" width="100" height="100">Get Started</h4>
<ul>
<li>Register for the hackathon on Devpost</li>
<li>Join the <a href="https://discord.gg/ujTrwKZsXz" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Discord support channel</a>
</li>
<li>Discover <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/collections/d4k8fy16ze8oyy?wt.mc_id=responsibleaihack_azure_content_wwl&ocid=AID3037981&utm_source=responsibleaihack" target="_blank" rel="noopener">basic concepts and learning opportunities</a> on how to build an intelligent app using Azure AI and Azure Databases (e.g. Azure Cosmos DB and Azure SQL) and additional Azure Services (e.g. Azure Functions, Azure Kubernetes Service)</li>
<li>Brainstorm with <a href="https://microsoftaiclassroom.devpost.com/details/ideagen" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Devpost’s Idea Generator</a>
</li>
<li>
<span>Request access to an </span><a href="https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students?wt.mc_id=responsibleaihack_azure_content_wwl&ocid=AID3037981&utm_source=responsibleaihack" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Azure for Students</span></a><span> account</span>
</li>
</ul>

<h5>What to Submit</h5>

The video should include an explanation of how your project uses Azure AI and Azure Data Services while highlighting how your project might reimagine the Future of Education. </p>

  "description": "<h4 id="chainlink-spring-2023-hackathon" class="h2-title"><span>CHAINLINK SPRING 2023 HACKATHON</span></h4>\n<p><span>Smart contract developers are reinventing applications in finance, gaming, insurance, art, and many more industries, creating a system that executes contracts based on mathematical certainty. Chainlink decentralized oracle networks are at the center of this evolution, enabling developers to leverage high-quality data from APIs and other data sources along with powerful off-chain computation resources to build the next generation of smart contract applications.</span></p>\n<p><span>Whether you need secure market data for a DeFi app, verifiable randomness for a blockchain-based game, or low-cost off-chain computation to automate various contract functions,&nbsp;</span><a href="https://blog.chain.link/how-chainlink-supports-any-off-chain-data-resource-and-computation/"><span>Chainlink’s flexible oracle infrastructure</span></a><span>&nbsp;provides developers with the extensive suite of decentralized services they need to build more feature-rich dApps.&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p>\n<p><span>This year’s Chainlink Spring 2023 Hackathon aims to empower developers of all skill levels to use Chainlink oracle networks to build decentralized applications that address a wide range of use cases and realize the full potential of hybrid smart contracts. Get hands-on experience with smart contracts, a fast onboarding to the Chainlink tech stack, workshops with top engineers, exposure to blockchain career opportunities, and a chance to win prizes from a total pool of $450k+</span></p>\n<p><span>Past Chainlink hackathons have seen individuals and teams build hybrid smart contract applications that have&nbsp;<a href="https://blog.chain.link/chainlink-fall-2022-hackathon-winners/">redefined what dApps can do</a>.</span><span>&nbsp;For this event, we want to see even more creative applications that leverage the full power of Chainlink solutions.&nbsp;</span></p>\n<p><span>Hackathon participants will have an entire month to explore, experiment, and build together, as well as the opportunity to meet top developers from Chainlink Labs, who will be available to check out their work, offer feedback, and give a behind-the-scenes glimpse of what it’s like to build at the cutting edge of the smart contract industry.</span></p>\n<p><span>The official hackathon runs from&nbsp;<strong><span>April 28th to June 9th, 2023</span></strong>. See below for more details about the event, including the prizes on offer and potential building opportunities.</span></p>\n<p>Some important reminders:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<span>Project submission dates</span>: April 28 - June 9 @ 11:45pm ET</li>\n<li>\n<a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IBMzkKl-7EI">Closing Ceremony</a>: June 24, 2022</li>\n<li>The Hackathon workshop schedule is available <a href="https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_cdcf555747d9116e6a3d634e020fe7e0677f0a7fae0f4dfcc360d971770e1a5c@group.calendar.google.com&amp;ctz">here</a>.&nbsp;<br><br>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h4 id="what-is-chainlink" class="h2-title"><span>WHAT IS CHAINLINK?</span></h4>\n<p><span>Chainlink is the industry standard for building, accessing, and selling oracle services needed to power hybrid smart contracts on any blockchain. Chainlink oracle networks provide smart contracts with a way to reliably connect to any external API and leverage secure off-chain computations for enabling feature-rich applications.</span></p>\n<p><a href="https://data.chain.link/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Chainlink Data Feeds</a><span>&nbsp;provide a large collection of streaming market data. Developers can currently integrate easy-to-deploy code to retrieve Data Feeds for crypto assets, commodities, FOREX, and more market data, opening up a huge number of potential applications.</span></p>\n<p><span>If you’re looking to call a specific API or type of data, build a straightforward&nbsp;</span><a href="https://blog.chain.link/rfid-blockchain-integration-with-chainlink-external-adapters/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>External Adapter</span></a><span>&nbsp;to call the API to your Solidity smart contract. Creating a new External Adapter is a fantastic hackathon project for those new to Chainlink, and can add a unique identity to projects from veteran smart contract developers.&nbsp;</span></p>\n<p><span>A popular solution for gaming, ticketing, and many other use cases,&nbsp;</span><a href="https://docs.chain.link/docs/chainlink-vrf/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Chainlink VRF</span></a><span>&nbsp;provides developers access to provably random numbers, enabling them to build any type of app that needs transparent and secure RNG (random number generation) on-chain.</span></p>\n<p><span>Chainlink Automation enables conditional execution of your smart contracts functions through a hyper-reliable and decentralized automation platform that uses the same external network of node operators that secures billions in value.</span></p>\n<p><span>Creativity is your only limiting factor—Chainlink empowers your smart contracts with any data source you can think of in a secure manner, allowing you to build end-to-end decentralized, secure, and reliable applications.</span></p>\n<h4 id="register-today-and-gear-up-with-chainlink-hackathon-resources" class="h2-title"><span>REGISTER TODAY AND GEAR UP WITH CHAINLINK HACKATHON RESOURCES</span></h4>\n<p><span>To help maximize the success of projects, hackathon participants will be provided with direct access to experienced mentors and technical support, extensive educational materials for learning about off-chain services, live workshops showcasing how to use Chainlink, and much more. We also encourage you to join the hackathon channel in the official&nbsp;</span><a href="https://discord.gg/h3AvTHj" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Chainlink Discord</span></a><span>&nbsp;to meet other hackers and to explore our collection of developer resources below:</span></p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p><a href="https://docs.chain.link/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Chainlink Docs</span></a></p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><a href="https://chain.link/bootcamp" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Smart Contract Developer Bootcamp On-Demand</span></a></p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M576WGiDBdQ&amp;feature=youtu.be" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>16-Hour Smart Contract Developer Course</span></a></p>\n</li>\n<li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyMwXuJrbJQ"><span><span>32 hour Smart Contract Developer course (JavaScript edition)</span></span></a></li>\n<li>\n<p><a href="https://docs.chain.link/docs/hackathon-resources/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Boilerplate, Starter Kits, and Tutorials</span></a></p>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<p><span>If you want to kickstart your blockchain development journey and #BuildWithChainlink to realize the full potential of hybrid smart contracts,&nbsp;<a href="https://chain.link/hackathon" target="_blank" rel="noopener">register today</a>&nbsp;to secure your spot today for the Chainlink Spring 2023 Hackathon. This is our biggest hackathon yet and is poised to spur a major wave of innovation across DeFi, the NFT economy, and the larger smart contract ecosystem. As always, we can’t wait to see what you build.</span></p>\n<p><strong><span>PS:</span></strong>&nbsp;<span>See the&nbsp;<span><a href="https://chainlinkspring2023.devpost.com/details/challenges" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Sponsor Challenges</a></span>&nbsp;</span><span>tab for details on the prize breakdown - each sponsor has its own challenge statement &amp; prize breakdown.&nbsp;</span></p>\n<p><strong>SWAG Disclaimer:&nbsp;</strong>Transportation companies are currently facing limitations when shipping items to Russia and Ukraine, and as such we won't be able to send the Chainlink Spring 2023 Hackathon SWAG to these countries.&nbsp;</p>",

      <article id="challenge-description">

  <h4 id="chainlink-spring-2023-hackathon" class="h2-title"><span>CHAINLINK SPRING 2023 HACKATHON</span></h4>
<p><span>Smart contract developers are reinventing applications in finance, gaming, insurance, art, and many more industries, creating a system that executes contracts based on mathematical certainty. Chainlink decentralized oracle networks are at the center of this evolution, enabling developers to leverage high-quality data from APIs and other data sources along with powerful off-chain computation resources to build the next generation of smart contract applications.</span></p>
<p><span>Whether you need secure market data for a DeFi app, verifiable randomness for a blockchain-based game, or low-cost off-chain computation to automate various contract functions, </span><a href="https://blog.chain.link/how-chainlink-supports-any-off-chain-data-resource-and-computation/"><span>Chainlink’s flexible oracle infrastructure</span></a><span> provides developers with the extensive suite of decentralized services they need to build more feature-rich dApps.  </span></p>
<p><span>This year’s Chainlink Spring 2023 Hackathon aims to empower developers of all skill levels to use Chainlink oracle networks to build decentralized applications that address a wide range of use cases and realize the full potential of hybrid smart contracts. Get hands-on experience with smart contracts, a fast onboarding to the Chainlink tech stack, workshops with top engineers, exposure to blockchain career opportunities, and a chance to win prizes from a total pool of $450k+</span></p>
<p><span>Past Chainlink hackathons have seen individuals and teams build hybrid smart contract applications that have <a href="https://blog.chain.link/chainlink-fall-2022-hackathon-winners/">redefined what dApps can do</a>.</span><span> For this event, we want to see even more creative applications that leverage the full power of Chainlink solutions. </span></p>
<p><span>Hackathon participants will have an entire month to explore, experiment, and build together, as well as the opportunity to meet top developers from Chainlink Labs, who will be available to check out their work, offer feedback, and give a behind-the-scenes glimpse of what it’s like to build at the cutting edge of the smart contract industry.</span></p>
<p><span>The official hackathon runs from <strong><span>April 28th to June 9th, 2023</span></strong>. See below for more details about the event, including the prizes on offer and potential building opportunities.</span></p>
<p>Some important reminders:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<span>Project submission dates</span>: April 28 - June 9 @ 11:45pm ET</li>
<li>
<a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IBMzkKl-7EI">Closing Ceremony</a>: June 24, 2022</li>
<li>The Hackathon workshop schedule is available <a href="https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_cdcf555747d9116e6a3d634e020fe7e0677f0a7fae0f4dfcc360d971770e1a5c@group.calendar.google.com&ctz">here</a>. <br><br>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="what-is-chainlink" class="h2-title"><span>WHAT IS CHAINLINK?</span></h4>
<p><span>Chainlink is the industry standard for building, accessing, and selling oracle services needed to power hybrid smart contracts on any blockchain. Chainlink oracle networks provide smart contracts with a way to reliably connect to any external API and leverage secure off-chain computations for enabling feature-rich applications.</span></p>
<p><a href="https://data.chain.link/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Chainlink Data Feeds</a><span> provide a large collection of streaming market data. Developers can currently integrate easy-to-deploy code to retrieve Data Feeds for crypto assets, commodities, FOREX, and more market data, opening up a huge number of potential applications.</span></p>
<p><span>If you’re looking to call a specific API or type of data, build a straightforward </span><a href="https://blog.chain.link/rfid-blockchain-integration-with-chainlink-external-adapters/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>External Adapter</span></a><span> to call the API to your Solidity smart contract. Creating a new External Adapter is a fantastic hackathon project for those new to Chainlink, and can add a unique identity to projects from veteran smart contract developers. </span></p>
<p><span>A popular solution for gaming, ticketing, and many other use cases, </span><a href="https://docs.chain.link/docs/chainlink-vrf/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Chainlink VRF</span></a><span> provides developers access to provably random numbers, enabling them to build any type of app that needs transparent and secure RNG (random number generation) on-chain.</span></p>
<p><span>Chainlink Automation enables conditional execution of your smart contracts functions through a hyper-reliable and decentralized automation platform that uses the same external network of node operators that secures billions in value.</span></p>
<p><span>Creativity is your only limiting factor—Chainlink empowers your smart contracts with any data source you can think of in a secure manner, allowing you to build end-to-end decentralized, secure, and reliable applications.</span></p>
<h4 id="register-today-and-gear-up-with-chainlink-hackathon-resources" class="h2-title"><span>REGISTER TODAY AND GEAR UP WITH CHAINLINK HACKATHON RESOURCES</span></h4>
<p><span>To help maximize the success of projects, hackathon participants will be provided with direct access to experienced mentors and technical support, extensive educational materials for learning about off-chain services, live workshops showcasing how to use Chainlink, and much more. We also encourage you to join the hackathon channel in the official </span><a href="https://discord.gg/h3AvTHj" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Chainlink Discord</span></a><span> to meet other hackers and to explore our collection of developer resources below:</span></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><a href="https://docs.chain.link/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Chainlink Docs</span></a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="https://chain.link/bootcamp" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Smart Contract Developer Bootcamp On-Demand</span></a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M576WGiDBdQ&feature=youtu.be" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>16-Hour Smart Contract Developer Course</span></a></p>
</li>
<li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyMwXuJrbJQ"><span><span>32 hour Smart Contract Developer course (JavaScript edition)</span></span></a></li>
<li>
<p><a href="https://docs.chain.link/docs/hackathon-resources/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Boilerplate, Starter Kits, and Tutorials</span></a></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p><span>If you want to kickstart your blockchain development journey and #BuildWithChainlink to realize the full potential of hybrid smart contracts, <a href="https://chain.link/hackathon" target="_blank" rel="noopener">register today</a> to secure your spot today for the Chainlink Spring 2023 Hackathon. This is our biggest hackathon yet and is poised to spur a major wave of innovation across DeFi, the NFT economy, and the larger smart contract ecosystem. As always, we can’t wait to see what you build.</span></p>
<p><strong><span>PS:</span></strong> <span>See the <span><a href="https://chainlinkspring2023.devpost.com/details/challenges" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Sponsor Challenges</a></span> </span><span>tab for details on the prize breakdown - each sponsor has its own challenge statement & prize breakdown. </span></p>
<p><strong>SWAG Disclaimer: </strong>Transportation companies are currently facing limitations when shipping items to Russia and Ukraine, and as such we won't be able to send the Chainlink Spring 2023 Hackathon SWAG to these countries. </p>
</article>

      
    <article id="challenge-requirements">
      <div class="section-title bold">
        <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
          Requirements
        </h3>
        <span class="section-title-line"></span>
      </div>

      <div>
        <p>Each project must use Chainlink in some form to make a state change on a blockchain, otherwise it will not be eligible for the Chainlink core prizes. This means that a front end simply reading from Chainlink data feeds <span>doesn't count</span>. Using one of Chainlink Data Feeds, Chainlink VRF, Chainlink Keepers, or Chainlink API Calls <span>inside your smart contracts </span>is required. </p>
<p>For sponsor prizes, you do not have to use Chainlink - but to make your project as best as it can be using the materials here, it is recommended you do!</p>
<p>Projects must have been created during the duration of the hackathon, and not previously. Improvements on existing projects are acceptable, so long as the improvement project is clearly stated.</p>
<p> </p>
<p><strong>*For Flow projects:</strong> Resources can be found at <a href="https://developers.flow.com/">https://developers.flow.com/</a></p>
<p><em><span>Because Chainlink services are not yet fully integrated into the Flow blockchain, we're making an exception for the state-changing requirement around Chainlink services for hackathon participants building on Flow. To be eligible for a Chainlink core and Flow hackathon prize, you must change the blockchain state on Flow AND read the result of a Chainlink service (e.g., price data) from another blockchain.</span></em></p>
<p><strong>* For Space and Time projects:</strong> please visit the <a href="https://github.com/SxT-Community/chainlink-hackathon/tree/main">onboarding page </a>for more information and resources</p>
<p><strong>*For Verse (Bitcoin.com) projects:</strong> please go to <a href="https://bitcoincom.notion.site/Application-Process-Guidelines-82de720af76940e5a1d447a916f34943">Verse Community Guidelines</a> for requirements and judging criteria</p>
      </div>
    </article>

      <article id="judging-criteria">
  <div class="section-title bold">
    <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
      Judging Criteria
    </h3>
    <span class="section-title-line"></span>
  </div>

  <ul class="no-bullet">
      <li>
        <strong>User Experience / User Interface</strong><br>
        How useable is your project? Does it look nice? Does it accomplish what it's set out to do in an easy to use and approachable way?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Originality / Uniqueness</strong><br>
        Has this project been done before? Is it unique?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Technicality</strong><br>
        How difficult is the problem you're solving? How many moving parts? Did you build it in an efficient manner? Did you give it too many moving parts? How clean is the code?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Practicality</strong><br>
        Is this something people will want to use? Does this have business value? Is this something that could grow and have a mass following?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Wow factor</strong><br>
        Buffer points for anything not captured in the above pieces of criteria!
      </li>
  </ul>
</article>

    <article id="challenge-requirements">
      <div class="section-title bold">
        <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
          Requirements
        </h3>
        <span class="section-title-line"></span>
      </div>

      <div>
        <h5>What to Build</h5>
<p>Build or update an app for Square sellers that uses both Square APIs and Google AI APIs. </p>
<h5>What to Submit</h5>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Square Application ID</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Google Cloud Project ID</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide access to working application (test account, website, sandbox / production) - Instructions must be provided for judges to access</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Include a video (about 3 minutes) that demonstrates your submission. Videos must be uploaded to YouTube or Vimeo and made public.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide a text description of your project that explains how the new features were implemented</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Identify which category you are submitting into</p>
<ul>
<li>reinvention or unification of in-person and online experiences</li>
<li>text or chat foundational model </li>
<li>image/audio model or combination of multiple modalities</li>
<li>positive social change</li>
<li>use of 1 or more of the following Square APIs: Terminal API, Subscriptions API, Invoices API</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h5>Submission Specifics</h5>
<ul>
<li>
<p>The Project must be capable of being successfully installed and must function as depicted in the video and/or expressed in the text description.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The Project must run on the platform for which is specified in the Submission Requirements. </p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The Entrant must make the Project available free of charge and without any restriction</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Multiple Submissions: An Entrant may submit more than one Submission, however, each submission must be unique and substantially different</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>All Submission materials must be in English</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Your complete submission form on Devpost before the final deadline.</p>
<p> </p>

      <article id="challenge-description">

  <h4 id="attend-live-workshops" class="h2-title">Attend Live Workshops </h4>
<p>Check out the full schedule <a href="https://docker.devpost.com/details/workshops">here</a>!</p>
<p> </p>
<h4 id="about-the-challenge" class="h2-title">About the challenge</h4>
<p>Docker and Docker Hub are the starting point for practitioners to start their AI/ML journey and distribute their applications or models. We’re looking for hacks that use Docker products to help both beginners and advanced users get inspired, get started, and be productive within this exciting new frontier.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4 id="get-started" class="h2-title">Get started</h4>
<p>1. Register for the hackathon to stay informed</p>
<p>2. Sign up for a <a href="docker.com">Docker</a> account</p>
<p>3. Go to the <a title="Idea Generator" href="https://docker.devpost.com/details/ideas" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Idea Generator</a> to start thinking about what to build</p>
<p>4. Join the #docker-ai-ml-hackathon channel in the <a href="https://dockr.ly/comm-slack">Docker Community Slack </a></p>
</article>

      
    <article id="challenge-requirements">
      <div class="section-title bold">
        <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
          Requirements
        </h3>
        <span class="section-title-line"></span>
      </div>

      <div>
        <h4>What to Build</h4>
<p><span>Create a working software application, non-code proof of concept, or design with a strong concept validation that uses AI/ML in conjunction with Docker technologies.</span></p>
<p>*We favor submissions that are as close to a real-world implementation as possible, but accept submissions that are not fully functional if they show a strong proof of concept.</p>
<h5>Examples:</h5>
<p><span></span></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>AI/ML projects or models built using Docker technology and distributed through DockerHub</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>AI/ML integrations into Docker products which improves the developer experience</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enhancement or extensions of Docker products which makes developer working with AI/ML more productive</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<h4>What to Submit</h4>
<ul>
<li>Project built with AI/ML and any Docker technology</li>
<li>URL to your app, non-code proof of concept, or design </li>
<li>Text description explaining the features and functionality of your Project currently or in future</li>
<li>3-5 minute demo video</li>
</ul>
      </div>
    </article>

5 Reasons private hackathons drive customer engagement

Hereâs how private customer hackathons reduce churn and drive revenue growth.

By
Stephanie Rochon
Content Marketing Manager at Devpost
Share:

In todayâs busy SaaS landscape, reducing churn and driving expansion with customers has the attention of every leadership team. To win in these areas, you need your customers' engineering teams to understand your product's full capability, experiment with new use cases, and provide your product team with actionable feedback.

Customer hackathons allow you to do all three. These events allow you to engage directly with customers and gain valuable insights along the way. Customer hackathons drive innovation and are key to long-term product adoption, improving customer retention, and well-trained customers. Let's dive into what you need to know about these impactful events.

What are private customer hackathons?

Private customer hackathons are competitions held by companies for a select group of their customers. Just like in a regular hackathon, participants are asked to experiment and build against a deadline. The biggest difference is who can attend, as participants are usually specifically invited and the results are typically not shared publicly.Â 

Why run customer hackathons?

Customer hackathons allow you to improve product adoption, drive revenue, reduce churn, and gather highly specific insights from your existing customers.

Companies like SAP run customer hackathons as a way to drive customer engagement.

âHackathons are extremely valuable for understanding the customer challenges in a short time, testing the practicality of the SAP service, and improving the functionalities and user experience,â said Nico Wyss, Solutions Advisor at SAP.

Customer hackathons help customers overcome the hurdle of learning or integrating your product. Read more about the ways these events can help you connect with customers and drive revenue.Â 

#1 Improve the customer onboarding process

You probably already provide training during customer onboarding. Why not make it a memorable experience for customers? Customer hackathons are a fun and effective way to train customers on using your platform. These events help customers learn more about your product, improve their skills, and find new ways to use it effectively.Â 

Through workshops, demos, and hands-on hackathons, customers enhance their skills and learn to use your platform in a way that caters to their needs. This unlocks additional value from your productâand further solidifies its place in their workflows.

#2 Get customers building with your tools

One of the best ways to sell your offering is to show your offering. Your prospects and customers are a lot more likely to use your product if they see exactly how it benefits them. While it sounds obvious in theory, actually getting customers to add your product to their workflows is another storyâwhich is where customer hackathons come in.

In private customer hackathons, you can customize demos and use cases to meet their specific needs and pain points. Your customers and prospects will be incentivized to learn or integrate your product, which goes a long way in building a loyal user base thatâll stick around for the long haul.

#3 Reduce churn

Churn is the enemy of any subscription-based business. However, ensuring your clients know your product and integrate it into their workflows is the key to reducing churn.

Hosting private customer hackathons reduces churn in a number of ways:

  • Enables customers to experiment with new use cases
  • Trains customers on your productâincluding ongoing training
  • Gets customers building with your tools
  • Fosters customer relationship-building
  • Allows you to collect valuable insights on product usage

{{callout-1}}

#4 Speed up sales cycles and drive faster revenue growth

At the end of the day, all these benefits of customer hackathons culminate in one overarching goal: driving revenue growth. Private customer hackathons let you choose participants from your target audience, including potential customers who are evaluating your product. Letting them try your product firsthand can help them make decisions faster than just hearing a sales pitch.

After the hackathon, you can capitalize on the momentum generated during the event and weave it into your follow-up strategy. Whether thatâs personalized follow-up emails, targeted content, or offering additional training, use the insights gained from your hackathon to show prospective customers exactly why they should work with you.

#5 Inspire innovation

Customer hackathons arenât just about training your customers. They're also about collaboration, ideation, and problem-solvingâfor customers and your colleagues. Getting your companyâs developers and product teams involved in the event gives them a chance to see firsthand how customers interact with the product. Not only can these insights inspire innovation among your team members, but customers who are challenged to use your product in a new way will likely uncover ideas for improvement or new features.

Improve customer experience with customer hackathons

Customer hackathons allow you to break the mold of a traditional sales pitch. Not only do they create a fun experience, but these events provide customers with real value as they learn how to solve their business challenges with your product.Â 

To give your customers the best experience possible, use a hackathon platform to make sure everything runs smoothly. A platform like Devpost for Teams (DFT) streamlines hackathon management for organizers and is easy for participants to use.

Nowâs the time to embrace the idea of customer hackathons and create a memorable, valuable experience. Your customersâand your bottom lineâwill thank you for it.

  <iframe type="text/html" width="100%" height="100%" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/4wVwtmjaHcE?enablejsapi=1&hl=en_US&rel=0&start=&version=3&wmode=transparent" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" frameborder="0" allowscriptaccess="always" webkitAllowFullScreen="true" wmode="transparent" mode="transparent" class="video-embed"></iframe>
</div>



  <p><span><span>Welcome to the PartyRock Generative AI Hackathon by AWS: a challenge for all builders to get hands-on making generative AI-powered apps. In this challenge, you’ll use PartyRock, an Amazon Bedrock Playground as a fast and fun way to learn about Prompt Engineering and Foundational Models (FMs) to build a functional app with generative AI. Experiment with prompts to build an app based on one of four challenge categories or Remix the featured Side Quest app for more ways to compete! </span></span></p>
<p><a href="https://partyrock.aws/guide/getStarted" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Get started</a> and join the <a href="https://discord.gg/suU8YX2rkx" target="_blank" rel="noopener">AWS Community Discord</a> to run your ideas by other hackers or to get help from the PartyRock team.</p>
<p><img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/AWS%20PartyRock/Disco-resource-300.png" alt="" width="300" height="300"></p>
</article>

      
    <article id="challenge-requirements">
      <div class="section-title bold">
        <h3 class="subheader section-title-left">
          Requirements
        </h3>
        <span class="section-title-line"></span>
      </div>

      <div>
        <h4>What to Create</h4>
<p>1. <strong>Create or Remix a PartyRock app</strong> to fit into <span style="text-decoration: underline;">one</span> of the following categories:</p>
<ul>
<li>Interactive Learning Experience - virtual science lab, language lesson, etc;</li>
<li>Creative Assistant - music composition assistance, story idea generator, etc;</li>
<li>Experimental Entertainment - interactive story, Role Playing Games, etc;</li>
<li>Freestyle - any project that doesn’t fall into one of the categories above.</li>
</ul>
<p><span><span> </span><strong>AND/OR</strong></span></p>
<p>2. <strong>Remix Side Quest:</strong> Remix THIS <a title="Remix THIS app" href="https://partyrock.aws/u/banjtheman/CnsW_HHSL/ChatRPG" target="_blank" rel="noopener">community-created ChatRPG app</a> to creatively transform it into something as far from the original as possible</p>
<h4> </h4>
<h4>What to Submit</h4>
<p><img src="https://devpost-public.s3.amazonaws.com/AWS%20PartyRock/Disco-list-real-final-300.png" alt=""></p>
<p>No matter which type of Project you submit, you’ll need to include the following: </p>
<ol>
<li>Link to your AWS PartyRock Project </li>
<li>Answer all submission questions</li>
<li>If applicable, link to your community.aws Blog Post (see details below) </li>
<li>Optional, but recommended: ~90-second demo video, record a short video interacting with the app you created on PartyRock. Check out the <a href="https://awspartyrockhackathon.devpost.com/details/inspiration#:~:text=the%20PartyRock%20team.-,INSPIRATION,-While%20a%20demo" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Inspiration tab</a> for ideas and tips on making an awesome demo video.</li>
</ol>
<p> </p>
<p><strong>Bonus: Blog Post Prize</strong> Share your journey and the wider impact of your work through a <a href="https://community.aws" target="_blank" rel="noopener">https://community.aws</a> blog post. Please use the tag '<span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>partyrock-hackathon</strong></span>' and address one or both of the following questions, offering valuable insights into your creative process and the potential influence of your project. The content of your blog post must be materially different than your submission questions. The first 152 Eligible Projects that post an Eligible Blog Post to community.aws. </p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Community Impact:</strong> Describe how your project can positively affect your target community. Discuss the potential benefits, envisioned real-world application, and any plans for encouraging adoption.</li>
<li><strong>Alternative Development Scenario with Amazon Bedrock:</strong> Outline how you would have developed your application using Amazon Bedrock if PartyRock wasn't available. Discuss architectural considerations, model selection, and integration of additional tools or services</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<p><strong>Feedback Survey Prize</strong> After you have experimented with PartyRock and submitted your Project, complete this <a href="https://challengepost.wufoo.com/forms/the-partyrock-gen-ai-hackathon-feedback-survey/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">feedback submission form</a> for a chance to win $500 in AWS Credits. </p>
<p> </p>
<p>See <a href="https://awspartyrockhackathon.devpost.com/rules" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Official Rules</a> for details. </p>

        <strong>Potential to Inspire</strong><br>
        Will the app inspire other users to make creative and entertaining apps?

      <li>
        <strong>Creativity</strong><br>
        How original is the idea? Does it address a potentially valuable use case?
      </li>
      <li>
        <strong>Entertainment Value</strong><br>
        Is the app engaging and fun to interact with?
      </li>
  </ul>

                    <h4 id="the-partyrock-generative-ai-hackathon-by-aws-the-hackathon-official-rules">The PartyRock Generative AI Hackathon by AWS (the “Hackathon”) Official Rules</h4>
<p>NO PURCHASE OR PAYMENT NECESSARY TO ENTER OR WIN. A PURCHASE OR PAYMENT WILL NOT INCREASE YOUR CHANCES OF WINNING. </p>
<p>SUBMISSION OF ANY ENTRY CONSTITUTES AGREEMENT TO THESE OFFICIAL RULES AS A CONTRACT BETWEEN ENTRANT (AND EACH INDIVIDUAL MEMBER OF ENTRANT), THE HACKATHON SPONSOR, AND DEVPOST.</p>
<p>THIS HACKATHON IS SUBJECT TO ALL FEDERAL, STATE, AND LOCAL LAWS AND IS VOID WHERE PROHIBITED BY LAW.</p>
<p><span style="       text-decoration: none;  ">These translations are provided for informational purposes only. In case of discrepancy, inconsistency, or conflict between this translation and the English version, the English version will prevail</span><span style="       text-decoration: none;  ">.</span></p>
<p><a href="https://awspartyrockhackathon.devpost.com/details/rulesinspanish"><span style="       text-decoration: underline;    ">Spanish Translation</span></a></p>
<p><span></span></p>
<p><a href="https://awspartyrockhackathon.devpost.com/details/rulesingerman"><span style="       text-decoration: underline;    ">German Translation</span></a></p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="1-dates-and-timing">1. Dates and Timing</h5>
<p><strong>Submission Period:</strong> January 29th, 2024 (10:00 am Pacific Time) – March 11th, 2024 (5:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Submission Period”).</p>
<p><strong>Feedback Period:</strong> January 29th, 2024 (10:00 am Pacific Time) – March 13th, 2024 (5:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Feedback Period”).</p>
<p><strong>Judging Period: </strong>March 20th, 2024 (10:00 am Pacific Time) – March 27th, 2024 (5:00 pm Pacific Time) (“Judging Period”).</p>
<p><strong>Winners Announced: </strong>On or around April 3rd, 2024 (2:00 pm Pacific Time).</p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="2-sponsor-and-administrator">2. Sponsor and Administrator</h5>
<p><strong>Sponsor:</strong> Amazon Web Services, 410 Terry Avenue North, Seattle, WA 98109-5210  </p>
<p><strong>Administrator:</strong> Devpost, Inc. (“Devpost”), 222 Broadway, Floor 19, New York, NY 10038</p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="3-eligibility">3. Eligibility</h5>
<p><em>* February 8, 2024: Update to eligibility: Participants must be at least 18 years of age at the time of entry. Participants from Mexico, the Philippines, Vietnam, Germany, Spain, and Argentina (excluding the listed regions) are allowed to enter.  </em></p>
<p><strong>The Hackathon IS open to: </strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Individuals who are at least the age of majority where they reside as of the time of entry (<span style="text-decoration: underline;">or, in any event, over the age of 18)</span>(“Eligible Individuals”);</li>
<li>Teams of Eligible Individuals (“Teams”); and</li>
<li>Organizations (including corporations, not-for-profit corporations, other nonprofit organizations, limited liability companies, partnerships, and other legal entities) that exist and have been organized or incorporated at the time of entry.</li>
</ul>
<p>(the above are collectively, “Entrants”)</p>
<p>An Eligible Individual may join more than one Team or Organization and an Eligible Individual who is part of a Team or Organization may also enter the Hackathon on an individual basis. If a Team or Organization is entering the Hackathon, they must appoint and authorize one individual (the “Representative”) to represent, act, and enter a Submission, on their behalf. By entering a Submission on behalf of a Team or Organization you represent and warrant that you are the Representative authorized to act on behalf of your Team or Organization.</p>
<p><strong>The Hackathon IS NOT open to: </strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Individuals who are residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, region, province, or territory where the laws of the United States or local law prohibits participating or receiving a prize in the Hackathon (including, but not limited to, <span style="text-decoration: underline;">the Argentinian provinces of Mendoza, Neuquén, Rio Negro, Salta, and Tierra del Fuego, Brazil, Crimea, Cuba, China France, Hong Kong, Italy, Iran, North Korea, the province of Quebec, Russia, Syria,</span> and any other country/region designated by the United States Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control) </li>
<li><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Individuals that are under the age of 18.</span></li>
<li>Organizations involved with the design, production, paid promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, including the Sponsor and Administrator (“Promotion Entities”).</li>
<li>Employees, representatives, and agents** of such Promotion Entities, and all members of their immediate family or household*</li>
<li>Any other individual involved with the design, production, promotion, execution, or distribution of the Hackathon, and each member of their immediate family or household*</li>
<li>Any Judge (defined below), or company or individual that employs a Judge</li>
<li>Any parent company, subsidiary, or other affiliate*** of any organization described above</li>
<li>Any other individual or organization whose participation in the Hackathon would create, in the sole discretion of the Sponsor and/or Administrator, a real or apparent conflict of interest </li>
<li>*The members of an individual’s immediate family include the individual’s spouse, children and stepchildren, parents and stepparents, and siblings and stepsiblings. The members of an individual’s household include any other person who shares the same residence as the individual for at least three (3) months out of the year. </li>
</ul>
<p><em>*Agents include individuals or organizations that in creating a Submission to the Hackathon, are acting on behalf of, and at the direction of, a Promotion Entity through a contractual or similar relationship.</em></p>
<p><em>**An affiliate is: (a) an organization that is under common control, sharing a common majority or controlling owner, or common management; or (b) an organization that has a substantial ownership in, or is substantially owned by the other organization.</em></p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="4-how-to-enter">4. How To Enter </h5>
<p>Entrants may enter by visiting <a title="Hackathon Official Website" href="https://www.AWSPartyRockHackathon.devpost.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener">AWSPartyRockHackathon.devpost.com</a> (“Hackathon Website”) and following the below steps:</p>
<ol>
<li>Register for the Hackathon on the Hackathon Website by clicking the “Join Hackathon” button. To complete registration, sign up to create a free Devpost account, or log in with an existing Devpost account. This will enable you to receive important updates and to create your Submission.</li>
<li>Entrants will obtain access to the required platform and complete a Project described below in Project Requirements. Use of the developer tools will be subject to the license agreement related thereto. Entry in the Hackathon constitutes consent for Devpost to collect and maintain an entrant’s personal information for the purpose of operating the Hackathon.</li>
<li>Sign up for an AWS PartyRock account using an Amazon, Google, or Apple account at <a title="PartyRock Official Site" href="http://www.partyrock.aws" target="_blank" rel="noopener">partyrock.aws</a>
</li>
<li>Complete and enter all of the required fields on the “Enter a Submission” page of the Hackathon Website (each a “Submission”) during the Submission Period and follow the requirements below.</li>
</ol>
<h5 id="project-requirements"><strong>Project Requirements</strong></h5>
<p><strong>What to Create: </strong>Entrants must Generate or Remix a PartyRock app to fit into one of the following categories (each a “Project”):</p>
<ul>
<li>Interactive learning experiences - virtual science labs, language lessons, etc;</li>
<li>Creative assistants - music composition assistance, story idea generators, etc;</li>
<li>Experimental entertainment - AI-driven interactive stories, RPGs, etc;</li>
<li>Freestyle - projects that do not fall into any of the categories above </li>
</ul>
<p><strong>AND/OR</strong></p>
<p><strong>Remix Side Quest:</strong> Remix the community-created ChatRPG app (THIS LINK: <a href="https://partyrock.aws/u/banjtheman/CnsW_HHSL/ChatRPG">https://partyrock.aws/u/banjtheman/CnsW_HHSL/ChatRPG</a>) to creatively transform it into something as far from the original as possible (see prize section 8 below for details).</p>
<p><em>**Sponsor and Administrator reserve the right to reassign a Project from one category to another if deemed more appropriate based on the content.</em></p>
<p><strong>Functionality: </strong>The Project must be capable of being successfully installed and running consistently on the platform for which it is intended and must function as depicted in the video and/or expressed in the text description.</p>
<p><strong>Platforms:</strong> A submitted Project must run on the platform for which it is intended and which is specified in the Submission Requirements. </p>
<p><strong>New & Existing:</strong> Only net-new OR Remixed applications (copies of existing PartyRock applications) that have been significantly updated during the Hackathon Submission Period are allowed. </p>
<p><strong>Third-Party Integrations:</strong> If a Project integrates any third-party SDK, APIs, and/or data, Entrant must be authorized to use them in accordance with any terms and conditions or licensing requirements of the tool.</p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="submission-requirements">Submission Requirements </h5>
<p>Submissions to the Hackathon must meet the following requirements:</p>
<ul>
<li>Must include a Project generated using AWS PartyRock and meets the above Project Requirements.</li>
<li>Must include a text description that explains the features, functionality, the intended purpose of your Project.</li>
<li>Should include a demonstration video of your Project. The video portion of the Submission:
<ul>
<li>should be less than ninety (90) seconds</li>
<li>should include footage that shows the intended interaction with your application </li>
<li>must be uploaded to and made publicly visible on YouTube, Vimeo, Facebook Video, or Youku, and a link to the video must be provided on the submission form on the Hackathon Website; and</li>
<li>must not include third-party trademarks, or copyrighted music or other material unless the Entrant has permission to use such material.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<strong>Remix Side Quest: </strong>Remix <a title="community-created ChatRPG" href="https://partyrock.aws/u/banjtheman/CnsW_HHSL/ChatRPG" target="_blank" rel="noopener">community-created ChatRPG</a> Submission Requirements
<ul>
<li>Must include a Remix of community-created ChatRPG app to creatively transform it into something as far from the original as possible (see Section 8. Prizes below for details) using AWS PartyRock and meets the above Project Requirements.</li>
<li>Must include a text description that explains the features, functionality, the intended purpose of your Project.</li>
<li>Should include a demonstration video of your Project. The video portion of the Submission:
<ul>
<li>should be less than ninety (90) seconds</li>
<li>should include footage that shows the intended interaction with the generated app </li>
<li>must be uploaded to and made publicly visible on YouTube, Vimeo, Facebook Video, or Youku, and a link to the video must be provided on the submission form on the Hackathon Website; and</li>
<li>must not include third-party trademarks, or copyrighted music or other material unless the Entrant has permission to use such material.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Blog Post Bonus Prize Submission Requirements</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Publish a blog post on https://community.aws about your project during the Submission Period.</li>
<li>Include a link to your published blog post on your Devpost Project submission form. The first 152 eligible posts will receive a Blog Post Bonus Prize. </li>
<li>Blog posts can cover similar topics but should be materially different than the Devpost text description.</li>
<li>Share your journey and the wider impact of your work through a community.aws blog post. Please use the tag 'partyrock-hackathon' and address one or both of the following criteria, offering valuable insights into your creative process and the potential influence of your project:
<ul>
<li>Community Impact: Describe how your project can positively affect your target community. Discuss the potential benefits, envisioned real-world application, and any plans for encouraging adoption.</li>
<li>Alternative Development Scenario with Amazon Bedrock: Outline how you would have developed your application using Amazon Bedrock if PartyRock wasn't available. Discuss architectural considerations, model selection, and integration of additional tools or services.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Feedback Prize Submission Requirements</strong></p>
<p>To be considered for the Most Valuable Feedback bonus prizes, participants must be registered for the hackathon on Devpost, have submitted a Project, and complete a feedback survey form (each a “Feedback Submission”). Feedback must be submitted during the Feedback Period. Participants must complete the survey with actionable comments that AWS PartyRock can use to improve the tool or related documentation (for example, bug reports, user interface improvements, suggested integrations, and more) and User Experience Reflection: Reflect on your experience using PartyRock. Highlight what you found beneficial and provide suggestions for improvements or new features to enhance user experience. One feedback form per entrant.</p>
<p><strong>Multiple Submissions: </strong>An Entrant may submit more than one Submission, however, each Submission must be unique and substantially different from each of the Entrant’s other Submissions, as determined by the Sponsor and Devpost in their sole discretion.</p>
<p><strong>Submission ownership:</strong> Be the original work of the Entrant, be solely owned by the Entrant, and not violate the Intellectual Property rights of any other person or entity.</p>
<p><strong>Testing: </strong>Access must be provided to an Entrant’s working Project for judging and testing by providing a link to a website, functioning demo, or a test build. If Entrant’s website is private, Entrant must include login credentials in its testing instructions. The Entrant must make the Project available free of charge and without any restriction, for testing, evaluation, and use by the Sponsor, Administrator, and Judges until the Judging Period ends. Judges are not required to test the Project and may choose to judge based solely on the text description, images, and video provided in the Submission.</p>
<p>Access can be provided to the Sponsor and Administrator by sharing a link to your newly generated or remixed PartyRock app.</p>
<p>If the Project includes software that runs on proprietary or third-party hardware that is not widely available to the public, including software running on devices or wearable technology other than smartphones, tablets, or desktop computers, the Sponsor and/or Administrator reserve the right, at their sole discretion, to require the Entrant to provide physical access to the Project hardware upon request.  </p>
<p><strong>Language Requirements: </strong>All Submission materials must be in English or, if not in English, the Entrant must provide an English translation of the demonstration video, text description, and testing instructions as well as all other materials submitted. </p>
<p><strong>Team Representation:</strong> If a team or organization is entering the Hackathon, they must appoint and authorize one individual (the “Representative”) to represent, act, and enter a Submission, on their behalf. The Representative must meet the eligibility requirements above. By entering a Submission on the Hackathon Website on behalf of a team or organization you represent and warrant that you are the Representative authorized to act on behalf of your team or organization.</p>
<p><strong>Intellectual Property: </strong>Your Submission must: (a) be your (or your Team, or Organization’s) original work product; (b) be solely owned by you, your Team, your Organization with no other person or entity having any right or interest in it; and (c) not violate the intellectual property rights or other rights including but not limited to copyright, trademark, patent, contract, and/or privacy rights, of any other person or entity. An Entrant may contract with a third party for technical assistance to create the Submission provided the Submission components are solely the Entrant’s work product and the result of the Entrant’s ideas and creativity, and the Entrant owns all rights to them. An Entrant may submit a Submission that includes the use of open source software or hardware, provided the Entrant complies with applicable open source licenses and, as part of the Submission, creates software that enhances and builds upon the features and functionality included in the underlying open source product. By entering the Hackathon, you represent, warrant, and agree that your Submission meets these requirements.</p>
<p><strong>Financial or Preferential Support:</strong> A Project must not have been developed, or derived from a Project developed, with financial or preferential support from the Sponsor or Administrator. Such Projects include, but are not limited to, those that received funding or investment for their development, were developed under contract, or received a commercial license, from the Sponsor or Administrator any time prior to the end of Hackathon Submission Period. The Sponsor, at their sole discretion, may disqualify a Project, if awarding a prize to the Project would create a real or apparent conflict of interest.</p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="5-submission-modifications">5. Submission Modifications</h5>
<p><strong>Draft Submissions: </strong>Prior to the end of the Submission Period, you may save draft versions of your submission on Devpost to your portfolio before submitting the Submission materials to the Hackathon for evaluation. Once the Submission Period has ended, you may not make any changes or alterations to your Submission, but you may continue to update the Project in your Devpost portfolio.</p>
<p><strong>Modifications:</strong> After the Submission Period. The Sponsor and Devpost may permit you to modify part of your Submission after the Submission Period for the purpose of adding, removing, or replacing material that potentially infringes a third-party mark or right, discloses personally identifiable information, or is otherwise inappropriate. The modified Submission must remain substantively the same as the original Submission with the only modification being what the Sponsor and Devpost permit. </p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="6-judges-criteria">6. Judges & Criteria</h5>
<p>Eligible submissions will be evaluated by a panel of judges selected by the Sponsor (the “Judges”). Judges may be employees of the sponsor or third parties, may or may not be listed individually on the Hackathon Website, and may change before or during the Judging Period. Judging may take place in one or more rounds with one or more panels of Judges, at the discretion of the sponsor. </p>
<p><strong>Stage One)</strong> The first stage will determine via pass/fail whether the ideas meet a baseline level of viability, in that the Project reasonably fits the theme and reasonably applies the required APIs/SDKs featured in the Hackathon.</p>
<p><strong>Stage Two)</strong> All Submissions that pass Stage One will be evaluated in Stage Two based on the following equally-weighted criteria (the “Judging Criteria”):</p>
<p>Entries will be judged on the following equally-weighted criteria, and according to the sole and absolute discretion of the judges:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Applicability</strong></li>
<li>Clarity of the use case (opportunity addressed)</li>
<li><strong>Quality of the Application</strong></li>
<li>How well does your app utilize the features of PartyRock and prompt engineering?</li>
<li><strong>Potential to Inspire</strong></li>
<li>Will the app inspire other users to make creative and entertaining apps?</li>
<li><strong>Creativity</strong></li>
<li>How original is the idea? Does it address a potentially valuable use case? </li>
<li><strong>Entertainment Value</strong></li>
<li>Is the app engaging and fun to interact with?</li>
</ul>
<p>The scores from the Judges will determine the potential winners of the applicable prizes. The Entrant(s) that are eligible for a Prize, and whose Submissions earn the highest overall scores based on the applicable Judging Criteria, will become potential winners of that Prize.</p>
<p><strong>Feedback Submission Criteria: </strong>Eligible Feedback Submissions will be evaluated based on the completeness, viability, and potential impact of the feedback.</p>
<p><strong>Tie Breaking: </strong>For each Prize listed below, if two or more Submissions are tied, the tied Submission with the highest score in the first applicable criterion listed above will be considered the higher-scoring Submission. In the event any ties remain, this process will be repeated, as needed, by comparing the tied Submissions’ scores on the next applicable criterion. If two or more Submissions are tied on all applicable criteria, the panel of Judges will vote on the tied Submissions.</p>
<p> </p>
<h5 id="7-intellectual-property-rights">7. Intellectual Property Rights</h5>
<p>All Submissions remain the intellectual property of the individuals or organizations that developed them. By submitting an entry, entrants agree that the Sponsor will have a fully paid, non-exclusive license to use such entry for judging the entry. Entrants agree that the sponsor and Devpost shall have the right to promote the Submission and use the name, likeness, voice, and image of all individuals contributing to a Submission, in any materials promoting or publicizing the Hackathon and its results, during the Hackathon Period and for three years thereafter.  Some Submission components may be displayed to the public. Other Submission materials may be viewed by the sponsor, Devpost, and judges for screening and evaluation. By submitting an entry or accepting any prize, entrants represent and warrant that (a) submitted content is not copyrighted, protected by trade secret, or otherwise subject to third-party intellectual property rights or other proprietary rights, including privacy and publicity rights, unless Entrant is the owner of such rights or has permission from their rightful owner to post the content; and (b) the content submitted does not contain any viruses, Trojan horses, worms, spyware or other disabling devices or harmful or malicious code.</p>
<p> </p>

<p><strong>IMPORTANT NOTES ON MULTIPLE PRIZE ELIGIBILITY:</strong></p>

<p><strong>Substitutions & Changes:</strong> Prizes are non-transferable by the winner. Sponsor in its sole discretion has the right to make a prize substitution of equivalent or greater value. <p><strong>Verification Requirement: </strong>THE AWARD OF A PRIZE TO A POTENTIAL WINNER IS SUBJECT TO VERIFICATION OF THE IDENTITY, QUALIFICATIONS AND ROLE OF THE POTENTIAL WINNER IN THE CREATION OF THE SUBMISSION. <p><strong>Prize Delivery:</strong> Prizes will be payable to the Entrant, if an individual; to the Entrant’s Representative, if a Team; or to the Organization, if the Entrant is an Organization. Failure to provide correct information on the Required Forms, or other correct information required for the delivery of a Prize, may result in delayed Prize delivery, disqualification of the Entrant, or forfeiture of a Prize.
